items.title: How Frank can restore reputation and save Crystal Palace
items.summary: Frank’s first job since Spurs dismissal in February He has been promised funds for January signings Thomas Frank has been confirmed as Crystal Palace’s manager after Pierre Sage was sacked last week. Frank, out of work since being dismissed by Tottenham in February, was quickly identified as Palace’s main target and has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal at the Premier League’s bottom club. Frank spoke to Palace in the summer about succeeding Oliver Glasner but decided he was not ready to return to the dugout because he wanted to take a break from football.

items.title: Vitor Matos: Strasbourg target Swansea City head coach
items.summary: Matos has indicated a desire for move to Ligue 1 Championship club would be due compensation Swansea City are increasingly resigned to their head coach, Vítor Matos, joining Strasbourg after he indicated a desire to join Chelsea’s sister club. The Ligue 1 club have approached Swansea with a view to Matos succeeding Hugo Oliveira. Strasbourg, acquired by Chelsea’s parent company BlueCo in 2023, have identified Matos as a replacement for Oliveira, who has won three of 10 league matches since succeeding Gary O’Neil in July.

items.title: ‘We want to win it’: Tuchel says Nations League can set up England for Euro 2028 glory
items.summary: Winning Nations League ‘the best preparation’ for Euros England to be seeded in Friday’s draw after Spain win Thomas Tuchel believes winning the Nations League would provide England with the springboard to Euro 2028 glory. The head coach watched his team close out the calendar year with a sensational 3-2 victory against Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium on ­Sunday. It meant England leapfrogged the world champions to finish top of their Nations League group and ensured seeded status for the ­quarter-final draw on Friday.

items.title: Record-breaking Andy Robertson is Scotland’s finest captain
items.summary: As he passes Kenny Dalglish’s appearance total, it is important to remember that it is the left-back’s journey that sets him apart Andy Robertson may not be Scotland’s greatest player, but he is indisputably their finest captain. It counts as sacrilege, even to generations who have watched Kenny Dalglish only on YouTube, to reputationally place Robertson above the Liverpool hero on the basis of a cap haul that will reach 103 in St Gallen on Monday. Dalglish’s international career ended at 102 and the curious events that meant he missed the 1986 World Cup.

items.title: Fifa accused of climate ‘record of failure’ due to Aramco deal and tournament expansion
items.summary: Groups question ‘sincerity’ to meet emissions pledges Oil giant is a major sponsor of football governing body The United Nations has been asked to review Fifa’s status as a signatory to a key environmental initiative, with complainants arguing football’s governing body has a “record of failure” on climate action. Fifa is a signatory to the UN’s Sports for Climate Action Framework, a coalition which seeks to persuade sporting organisations to “work together to achieve a climate-resilient future”. Under the framework, signatories agree to cut their greenhouse gas emissions by 50% by 2030 and to “partner with key stakeholders to deliver joint climate action”.

items.title: Pochettino: I’d tell Guardiola to ‘take it’ if he’s offered US coaching job
items.summary: As he prepares to depart for Manchester United, the outgoing US coach held court on a number of topics, including what he’d change about soccer in America Outgoing US head coach Mauricio Pochettino and former Manchester City head coach Pep Guardiola have a long, storied past. The two faced each other as players, when Guardiola was at Barcelona and Pochettino was making his name across town at Espanyol. They faced each other 22 times as managers in the Premier League and the two share a mutual respect – and intensity – when it comes to their approach to playing and coaching alike.

Brajan Gruda contributed a goal and two assists, with Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck also on the scoresheet as the hosts delivered their most impressive display so far under Jürgen Klopp’s leadership.

items.summary: Another 3-2 win in Spain brings the lure of a golden new hyper-future – but it did not pan out that way last time I may have the body of a weak and feeble German, but I have the heart and stomach of a manager of England. And I think it foul scorn that Spain should dare to invade the borders of my realm. Or, for that matter, any one of 24 qualified teams for Euro 2028, because at the end of the day there are no easy games at this level, I’ve always said that.

items.title: Spain in pain as historic run ends but De la Fuente feels best is yet to come
items.summary: While the head coach, players and Spanish press were magnanimous in defeat, there was pride mixed in with disappointment – and confidence the future is still bright “With every game, defeat gets closer,” Luis de la Fuente had said and on Sunday night it finally came. Spain had lost only one competitive game since Scotland in March 2023 back when the coach hadn’t won anything and didn’t look like he ever would – and that solitary loss was on penalties in the 2025 Nations League final . Statistically, they said, penalties don’t count, so while Portugal lifted the trophy that night, the team that won the European Championship and World Cup in the summers either side also claimed a Fifa record of 44 official games unbeaten.

items.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
items.summary: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations.

items.title: French football head Philippe Diallo to fight Infantino for Fifa presidency
items.summary: Diallo confirmed by Uefa as its chosen candidate He accused Infantino of seriously damaging football The French Football Federation president, Philippe Diallo, has been confirmed as Uefa’s surprise late choice to run for the Fifa presidency. The search for a Uefa-backed candidate to challenge Gianni Infantino was taken to the wire, with Wednesday the deadline for those planning to contest the Fifa election in March. “At a meeting held today and chaired by Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin, the national associations represented on the Uefa executive committee and the Fifa council invited Philippe Diallo, president of the French Football Federation (FFF), to stand as a candidate in the Fifa presidential election in March 2027 and unanimously pledged their full support,” a statement said.

items.title: Union of European Clubs escalates fight for football influence with formal complaint
items.summary: Body of 138 members complains to European Commission Uefa and the European Football Clubs power targeted The Union of European Clubs has submitted a formal complaint against the stranglehold Uefa and European Football Clubs maintain on football within the continent, dramatically escalating its efforts to obtain recognition by governing bodies and dilute the power held by the elite. The complaint, filed to the European Commission on Monday, challenges the memorandum of understanding (MoU) between EFC and Uefa. That agreement, which runs until July 2033, stipulates that EFC is the “sole body” representing European clubs.

items.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
items.summary: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup.

items.title: European football body’s plan to go global leaves Fifa on tenterhooks
items.summary: Findings of ‘feasibility study’ into quest for world domination loom with Europe’s wealthiest certain to benefit whatever the outcome It will be one of the most eagerly devoured documents in football circles, assuming its contents are ever fully revealed. In September, the increasingly powerful European Football Clubs body announced a “feasibility study” into how it can become established on a more global scale, morphing into an organisation that represents clubs all over the world. The study’s findings could, some leading figures in the sport’s governance believe, define football’s long-term future.
